If you could go back to the early days of the internet, would you handle privacy differently? Most of us would. We would be more careful about the services we used and the information we shared. Since time machines don't exist, we have to face reality as it is now. Your personal data is being sold publicly at this very moment.

Right now, your phone number, email address, home address, even family relationships, are all being packaged and sold to marketing companies, insurance firms, and hackers. While Safari and the Mail app have built-in privacy protections that can block some tracking when you browse the web, they cannot undo the damage of data collected over the years and spread across hundreds of broker databases. Data brokers have built a multi-billion dollar industry devoted to harvesting your digital data, packaging it, and reselling it. It's time to take your personal information off the market and off the internet. Here's how.

The security risks posed by the data broker industry

But the danger goes far beyond annoying spam calls. When your data is everywhere, you become an easy target for sophisticated cyber threats. Because this industry is essentially unregulated, your most private information and details—including past employment, places you've lived, previous loan records—can be purchased with ease. This represents a massive security concern.

Modern scammers use the data held by brokers to craft highly personalised (and hard-to-spot) phishing attacks. When scammers already know your job title, where you've lived, or the names of your colleagues and friends, they can easily bypass your instinctive defences. If a fraudster knows a great deal about you, the moment your guard drops, they have a very good chance of succeeding.

For those concerned about personal safety, these websites and brokers function as open, searchable databases that serve as tools for stalkers and harassers. By mapping the network of relationships between your friends, family, and neighbours, brokers provide a blueprint for locating anyone trying to keep a low profile and stay out of the spotlight.

The solution: Automated data removal with Incogni

The scale of this ecosystem is shocking, and frankly, demoralising. Trying to manually request removal from hundreds of websites one by one is essentially a full-time job, with a success rate close to zero—because if it were easy, these brokers would have gone out of business long ago. What you need is a solution that understands how this industry works and can help you reclaim your right to privacy.

That's why a service like Incogni has become essential to your life—both digital and physical. It turns a massive problem (your data being everywhere and sold indiscriminately) into a solved one, offering a one-stop solution. Rather than spending months tracking down brokers yourself, Incogni handles the tedious, repetitive administrative work of opt-out requests on your behalf. They make sure your data isn't just deleted once, but continuously prevent brokers from trying to re-collect and re-enter it.

Incogni's comprehensive dashboard lets you track the progress of your personal data removal in real time, including:

  • The number of databases that may hold your data
  • Removal requests being sent on your behalf
  • Completed removals and ongoing follow-up work

The practical benefits of data removal for privacy-conscious individuals

Getting delisted from internet broker databases delivers immediate results for you and your family

  • When companies can't purchase your number, scam calls and spam texts will decrease.
  • Scammers lose their leads. Identity thieves often obtain victim information from broker websites.
  • Your home address stays private, making it harder for stalkers and harassers to locate your residence.
  • Your credit score stays healthy, as reducing data exposure lowers the risk of identity theft and comprehensively safeguards your financial wellbeing.
